1.title: Secure Workloads and Applications
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Secure Workloads and Applications. This module covers task statement one point two. You will design the network layout of a V P C, control traffic with security groups and network A C L s, protect the edge with Shield and W A F, keep credentials out of code, give users a way to sign in, and secure the links between your sites and A W S. The exam describes a threat or a requirement, and asks you to choose the layer and the service.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Design a V P C with subnets, route tables, security groups, network A C L s and N A T gateways. Choose a segmentation strategy with public and private subnets, and private paths to A W S services. Integrate Shield, W A F, Secrets Manager and sign-in services to secure applications. Pick the right detection service: GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective or Security Hub. And secure external connections with V P N and Direct Connect.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Locks the Shop
1.text: Lantern and Loom is now busy, and the doors are open too wide. Bots scrape the listings, and a flood of requests slowed the shop for an hour. A developer left S S H open to the whole internet, and the database password sits in the source code. Customers need to sign in, and the team needs a private link to a partner's inventory system. Your job is to close each door, one layer at a time.

1.title: Threats and Defense in Depth
1.text: Start with the threats, and match each one to a layer. At the edge, you face D D o S floods, S Q L injection and scraping bots; the controls are Shield and W A F. In the network, open ports and unwanted traffic are handled by subnets, security groups, network A C L s and Network Firewall. In the workload, weak credentials and vulnerable software are handled by roles, Secrets Manager and Inspector. For identity, stolen or shared logins are handled by I A M, Cognito and M F A. And for detection, GuardDuty, Detective and Security Hub find attacks already underway. This is defense in depth: no single control is enough. Exam tip: match the threat to the layer first.

1.title: A Secure VPC Layout
1.text: Here is the standard secure layout. Public subnets hold the load balancer and the N A T gateway, and they have a route to the internet gateway. Private subnets hold the application servers, and they reach out only through N A T. Isolated subnets hold the database, with no route outside the V P C. Each subnet sits in one Availability Zone, so repeat the tiers in at least two zones. The figure shows the three tiers stacked in two zones, with the path of the traffic. Exam tip: only what must face the internet goes in a public subnet; everything else goes in private ones.

1.title: Subnet Types and Route Tables
1.text: What makes a subnet public, private or isolated? Its routes. A public subnet has a direct route to an internet gateway; it typically holds load balancers and N A T gateways. A private subnet has no direct route to an internet gateway, and uses a N A T device to reach the internet; it holds application servers. An isolated subnet has no routes outside the V P C; it holds databases. A V P N-only subnet has a route to a V P N connection through a virtual private gateway, for a private office link. Every subnet has one route table, the main one by default, and one network A C L. Exam tip: what makes a subnet public is its route to an internet gateway, not its name.

1.title: Security Groups
1.text: A security group is a virtual firewall for the resources it is attached to, such as E C two instances and load balancers. It is stateful, so return traffic for an allowed request is allowed automatically. It has allow rules only: there is no deny rule, and traffic that no rule allows is blocked. A rule's source can be an I P, short for Internet Protocol, range, or another security group, so you can chain the load balancer, application and database tiers. Open S S H and R D P only to specific ranges, never to everywhere. Rules match protocols, ports and source, and security groups have no additional charge. Exam tip: security groups are the main control, and they can only allow.

1.title: Network ACLs
1.text: A network A C L allows or denies traffic at the subnet level. It is stateless: a rule that allows inbound traffic does not allow the response, so you must allow the return traffic too. Rules are numbered and evaluated from the lowest number, and the first match applies. Rules can allow or deny. Every subnet has exactly one network A C L, and the default one allows all traffic. The best use is as an extra layer, or as a deny for a known bad address range. Exam tip: to block a specific address range, use a network A C L deny rule, because a security group cannot deny.

1.title: Security Group or Network ACL?
1.text: The exam loves this comparison. A security group applies to a resource's network interface; a network A C L applies to a subnet. A security group is stateful; a network A C L is stateless. A security group has allow rules only; a network A C L allows and denies. A security group evaluates all its rules together; a network A C L evaluates in number order and stops at the first match. A new security group allows no inbound traffic and all outbound; the default network A C L allows everything. Use security groups for tier-to-tier access, and network A C L s as an extra layer or for blocking ranges. Exam tip: stateful and allow-only on the resource is a security group.

1.title: NAT Gateways and Outbound-Only Access
1.text: A public N A T gateway lets instances in private subnets reach the internet, but nothing outside can start a connection to them. It sits in a public subnet, has an Elastic I P address, and the private subnets' route table points to it. A zonal N A T gateway lives in one Availability Zone, so use one per zone for resilience. A private N A T gateway links to other V P C s or on-premises networks, and has no Elastic I P. For I P version six, use an egress-only internet gateway. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, the documentation also describes a Regional N A T gateway, so check that page. Exam tip: private servers that must reach out but never be reached need a N A T gateway in a public subnet.

1.title: VPC Endpoints: Private Paths to AWS Services
1.text: How do private servers reach A W S services without the internet? With V P C endpoints. A gateway endpoint works through a route table entry and is not Private Link; it supports S three and Dynamo D B. An interface endpoint puts network interfaces with private I P addresses in your subnets, powered by Private Link; it covers many A W S services, plus your own or partner services. Traffic stays on the A W S network, not the public internet, and an endpoint policy controls which principals can use it. Without an endpoint, service endpoints are public, reached through the internet gateway or N A T. Exam tip: private S three or Dynamo D B access means a gateway endpoint; most other services use an interface endpoint.

2.title: Edge Protection with AWS WAF
2.text: A W S W A F is a web application firewall for H T T P and H T T P S requests, at layer seven. You attach a web A C L to CloudFront, an Application Load Balancer, A P I, short for application programming interface, Gateway, AppSync or a Cognito user pool. Rules match I P addresses, headers, query strings, the body or geography, and they allow, block or count. Managed rule groups cover common threats such as S Q L injection and cross-site scripting. Rate-based rules limit floods of requests from one source. A blocked request gets an H T T P four hundred three response, or a custom one. Exam tip: S Q L injection, scripting or bots against a web app means W A F, on CloudFront or the load balancer.

2.title: DDoS Protection with AWS Shield
2.text: A W S Shield protects against D D o S attacks. Shield Standard is automatic, with no extra charge, and protects against common network and transport attacks. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription with expanded detection and mitigation, expert help, and a subscription that covers the standard W A F fees for the resources it protects. It protects CloudFront, Route fifty-three, Global Accelerator, load balancers and Elastic I P addresses. The attack classes are volumetric attacks at layer three, protocol attacks at layer four, such as a S Y N flood, and application attacks at layer seven, such as request floods. Exam tip: free and automatic is Standard; extra protection, expert help and W A F fees covered is Advanced.

2.title: AWS Firewall Manager and AWS Network Firewall
2.text: Two firewall services solve different problems. A W S Firewall Manager lets you set protections once and apply them across the accounts in Organizations, including new accounts and new resources. It covers W A F, Shield Advanced, security groups, network A C L s and Network Firewall. A W S Network Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall and intrusion prevention service for a V P C. It filters traffic at the V P C perimeter, with Suricata-compatible rules, domain filtering and deep packet inspection. It uses firewall endpoints in their own subnets, and route tables send traffic through them. Exam tip: one policy for every account is Firewall Manager; deep inspection in the traffic path is Network Firewall.

2.title: Threat Detection: GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective and Security Hub
2.text: Four services help you find problems. Amazon GuardDuty detects threats from CloudTrail events, V P C flow logs and D N S logs, and needs no agents for those base feeds. Amazon Inspector scans E C two instances, container images and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities. Amazon Detective investigates findings by building a behavior graph that points to the root cause. A W S Security Hub gives you one view of findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie, plus checks against security standards. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, the documentation calls the posture service Security Hub C S P M, so check which name you see. Exam tip: detect with GuardDuty, scan with Inspector, investigate with Detective, aggregate with Security Hub.

2.title: Application Credentials: Secrets Manager and Parameter Store
2.text: Never hard-code credentials. Secrets Manager is for secrets such as database credentials, A P I keys and tokens. It rotates them automatically with a Lambda function, always encrypts with K M S, short for Key Management Service,, and charges per secret and per call. Parameter Store is for configuration, such as endpoints, machine image identifiers and flags. It has no rotation, optional encryption with a SecureString parameter, and a free standard tier. Replace hard-coded credentials with a runtime call, allowed by the application's I A M role. For A W S access, use roles; for keys, K M S; and for certificates, Certificate Manager. Exam tip: a secret that must rotate automatically means Secrets Manager.

2.title: Amazon Cognito for Application Users
2.text: Amazon Cognito has two parts that answer two questions. A user pool answers: who is this user? It is a user directory for sign-up and sign-in, issues tokens, adds multi-factor authentication, and federates social, S A M L and Open I D Connect providers. An identity pool answers: what A W S resources may this user reach? It swaps a trusted token for temporary A W S credentials, through S T S, and can even serve guests. Use both together for sign-in and direct access to services such as S three. The figure shows the four steps: sign in, receive tokens, exchange them for temporary credentials, and call S three. An A W S W A F web A C L can also protect a user pool. Exam tip: sign-in for customers is a user pool; direct A W S access for them adds an identity pool.

2.title: Choosing the Sign-In Service
2.text: Here is the chooser. Employees going to A W S accounts and A W S managed applications use I A M Identity Center. Customers of a web or mobile app use a Cognito user pool. App users who need temporary A W S credentials add a Cognito identity pool. Windows or L D A P applications that need a directory use A W S Directory Service. Servers and functions calling A W S use I A M roles. And database passwords an app reads at run time live in Secrets Manager. Exam tip: employees, Identity Center; customers, Cognito; code, roles.

2.title: Site-to-Site VPN and Client VPN
2.text: Now the external connections. Site-to-Site V P N is an I P sec connection between a V P C and your own network. Each connection has two tunnels, the A W S side is a virtual private gateway or a transit gateway, and your side is a customer gateway device. Client V P N is a managed, client-based V P N for individual users. They connect with Open V P N clients over T L S, sign in with Active Directory, S A M L or certificates, and authorization rules control what they reach. Exam tip: an office network to a V P C is Site-to-Site V P N; individual remote users use Client V P N.

2.title: AWS Direct Connect
2.text: A W S Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection from your site to an A W S Direct Connect location, bypassing internet providers. You create virtual interfaces: private for a V P C, public for public services such as S three, and transit for transit gateways. It gives consistent network performance. But it is not encrypted by default. To encrypt, add MACsec on supported connections, or run an I P sec V P N over Direct Connect. Build resilience with a second connection, or a V P N as a backup, as the figure shows with its dashed path. Exam tip: private and consistent is Direct Connect; private, consistent and encrypted adds a V P N or MACsec.

2.title: Choosing an External Connection
2.text: Choosing the link is a matter of keywords. A quick, encrypted link over the internet is Site-to-Site V P N. Consistent bandwidth and a private path is Direct Connect. Private, consistent and encrypted is Direct Connect with a V P N, or MACsec. Individual remote staff use Client V P N. For high availability, use two V P N tunnels, and a second connection or a V P N backup. Exam tip: look for the words encrypted, consistent and individual users.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Secure Workloads
2.text: Here is what the exam asks about secure workloads. Which network control: a subnet type, a security group, a network A C L, a N A T gateway or an endpoint. Which edge service: W A F, Shield, Firewall Manager or Network Firewall. Which detection service: GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective or Security Hub. Which credential store: Secrets Manager or Parameter Store. And which sign-in or link: Cognito, Identity Center, V P N or Direct Connect. Exam tip: name the threat or the traffic path first, then pick the layer.

3.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Locks the Shop
3.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Bots and S Q L injection against the storefront: W A F with managed and rate-based rules. A flood of requests slowed the shop: Shield, with Advanced for expert help. S S H open to the world: a security group limited to specific ranges. Block one hostile address range: a network A C L deny rule. App servers need updates but no inbound traffic: a N A T gateway in a public subnet. App servers read S three privately: a gateway endpoint. The database password in the code: Secrets Manager with rotation. Customers sign in and upload photos: Cognito user and identity pools. And the private link to the partner: Site-to-Site V P N, or Direct Connect with a V P N.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Here is the recap. For the layout, use public, private and isolated subnets across two Availability Zones. For traffic, security groups are stateful and allow only, network A C L s are stateless and allow and deny; use N A T for outbound access and endpoints to reach A W S services. At the edge, W A F handles web exploits, Shield handles D D o S, and Firewall Manager covers every account. To detect and protect, use GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective and Security Hub, with Secrets Manager for secrets. For access, use Cognito, Identity Center, V P N and Direct Connect.

3.title: Practice Question 1
3.text: Question one. Select two. Which two statements about security groups and network A C L s are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and D. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for allowed requests is allowed, and they have allow rules only. Network A C L s are stateless, apply at the subnet level, and can allow or deny, in rule-number order.

3.title: Practice Question 2
3.text: Question two. Lantern and Loom's application servers run in private subnets. They must download operating system patches from the internet, and nothing on the internet may start a connection to them. What should the architect add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: a N A T gateway in a public subnet, routed from the private subnets. It allows outbound connections while blocking unsolicited inbound ones. A direct internet gateway route or public addresses would expose the servers.

3.title: Practice Question 3
3.text: Question three. Lantern and Loom sees a flood of unwanted requests from one known address range, and wants to block it for every instance in a public subnet. Which is the simplest control? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: a network A C L rule that denies the address range. A network A C L applies to the subnet and supports deny rules. Security groups have only allow rules, and I A M policies control A P I access, not network traffic.

3.title: Practice Question 4
3.text: Question four. Lantern and Loom's storefront runs behind an Application Load Balancer. It must be protected against S Q L injection and against floods of requests from single I P addresses. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: an A W S W A F web A C L with managed rules and a rate-based rule. Managed rule groups cover S Q L injection, and rate-based rules limit floods from one source. Shield protects against D D o S, and GuardDuty detects but does not block.

3.title: Practice Question 5
3.text: Question five. Application servers in private subnets read product images from Amazon S three. Policy says this traffic must not cross the public internet or use a N A T gateway. What should the architect create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: a gateway V P C endpoint for S three, with a route table entry. It sends S three traffic over the A W S network. A N A T gateway uses the internet path, and an internet gateway would expose the subnets.

3.title: Practice Question 6
3.text: Question six. Lantern and Loom's code has the database password written in a configuration file. The team wants to remove it from the code and rotate it automatically on a schedule. Which service should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A W S Secrets Manager, with automatic rotation. The application fetches the credential at run time. Parameter Store has no rotation, K M S manages keys, and Cognito handles application users.

3.title: Practice Question 7
3.text: Question seven. Select two. Which two statements about A W S Shield are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Shield Standard is automatic and free. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription with expanded protection, and it covers the standard W A F fees for the resources it protects. S Q L injection is a W A F matter, and Shield does not replace security groups.

3.title: Practice Question 8
3.text: Question eight. Lantern and Loom wants to detect unusual A P I calls, contact with known malicious addresses and possible credential compromise across its accounts, without installing agents. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Amazon GuardDuty. It analyzes CloudTrail events, V P C flow logs and D N S logs with threat intelligence. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Config records configuration, and Detective investigates findings afterward.

3.title: Practice Question 9
3.text: Question nine. Lantern and Loom's new mobile app must let customers sign in with a social account, and then upload photos directly to an Amazon S three bucket with temporary credentials. Which design fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: a Cognito user pool for sign-in and a Cognito identity pool for temporary A W S credentials. I A M users and embedded keys are long-term credentials, and Identity Center is for the workforce.

3.title: Practice Question 10
3.text: Question ten. A company needs a private connection to A W S with consistent network performance, and the traffic must be encrypted in transit. Which design meets both needs? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S Direct Connect with a Site-to-Site V P N over it. Direct Connect gives a private, consistent path, but it does not encrypt traffic by default, so a V P N or MACsec adds encryption.

3.title: Answers at a Glance
3.text: Here are all ten answers. Question one: A and D. Question two: B. Question three: D. Question four: A. Question five: C. Question six: B. Question seven: A and C. Question eight: D. Question nine: A. Question ten: C. In Module three, we protect the data itself: encryption, keys, backups, retention and compliance.
